title: Finding your way
goals: Ask if there is a place nearby with Is there…? and Are there any…?, and answer with one, some or any.
Say where something is with next to, between, across from, on the corner of, behind…
Offer help and ask for favors with Can I…? Can you…? Could you…?
Give and understand directions: turn right, go straight ahead, walk north for two blocks.
Name places and stores in a city and describe what a neighborhood is like.
Check what you did not understand with Did you say…? and echo questions (It's where?).

learn.title: Is there…? / Are there any…?
learn.html:
To ask if something exists in a place, we use there is / there are (in Spanish, «hay»).

QuestionAnswer
SingularIs there a café near here?Yes, there is. There's one on Main Street.
No, there isn't. There isn't one in this neighborhood.
PluralAre there any cash machines near here?Yes, there are. There are some outside the bank.
No, there aren't. There aren't any nearby.
  • a / an + singular noun; any + plural noun in questions and negatives; some in positive sentences.
  • one replaces a singular noun that was already mentioned; some / any replace a plural one.
  • Short forms: there's, there isn't, there aren't.

watch.right: Is there a bank near here?
watch.why: «There» is always needed for «there is / there are». Do not leave it out.

watch.wrong: Are there some parks near here?
watch.right: Are there any parks near here?
watch.why: In questions, use any, not some.

learn.title: Where is it: place prepositions
learn.html:
To say where a place is, we use these expressions.

ExpressionMeaningExample
next tobesideThe bank is next to the café.
between … and …in the middle of two thingsThe café is between the bank and the drugstore.
across from / oppositeon the other side of the streetThe museum is across from the park.
in front of / behindbefore / after somethingThere's a bus stop in front of the school.
on the corner of … and …at the corner ofIt's on the corner of Main and First.
on + streeton (the street)There's a deli on Oak Street.
near here / around hereclose to hereIs there a bank around here?
inside / outsidein / out of a buildingThere are two ATMs outside the bank.

Look at this: next to, in front of, across from and on the corner of end with to / of / from; you cannot leave them out.

watch.right: The bank is on Main Street.

watch.right: The café is in front of the bank.

watch.right: The café is between the bank and the drugstore.

learn.title: Offering and asking with Can and Could
learn.html:
Can and could are used to offer help and to ask for favors. After them, use the verb in its base form, without to.

FunctionStructureExample
OfferCan I + verb…?Can I help you?
Offerwh- word + can I + verb…?How can I help? / What can I do?
AskCan you + verb…?Can you tell me how to get to the aquarium?
Ask (more polite)Could you + verb…?Could you give me directions, please?

Could you…? sounds more polite than Can you…?; use it with strangers. Answer with: Sure. / Of course. / Sorry, I'm not from here.

watch.why: After could, use the base form, without to.

watch.wrong: Do you can give me directions?
watch.why: Can does not use do in questions.

watch.wrong: Can you say me how to get to the museum?
watch.right: Can you tell me how to get to the museum?

learn.title: Giving directions: the imperative
learn.html:
To say how to get somewhere, we use the imperative: the verb in its base form, without a subject.

VerbExample
turn right / leftTurn left on Oak Street.
make a right / a leftAt the corner, make a right.
go straight aheadGo straight ahead for three blocks.
go down the streetGo down this street to the end.
walk + north / south / east / westWalk north for two blocks.
continue + direction + on + streetContinue east on Main Street.
walk back toWalk back to the entrance.
  • Amount: go two blocks (plural).
  • Streets: on Pine Avenue; corner: at the corner; end: at the end of the street.
  • Useful ending: You can't miss it. It's on the right.
  • Negative: Don't turn left; turn right.

watch.wrong: Walk to north for two blocks.
watch.why: North is an adverb: no to.

watch.wrong: Go two block and turn right.
watch.right: Go two blocks and turn right.
watch.why: After two, the noun is plural.

watch.wrong: You turn right at the corner.
watch.why: For directions, use the imperative, without you.

learn.title: Checking what you heard
learn.html:
If you do not understand a direction well, do not pretend: ask again.

  • Excuse me? / I'm sorry? — ask someone to repeat.
  • Did you say fifteen or fifty? — confirm between two options.
  • What did you say? — ask someone to repeat what they said.
  • Repeat one word with a question intonation: Within walking distance?
  • Echo questions: repeat the sentence and replace the part you did not hear with a question word: There's a Vietnamese place where? / It opens at what time? / A what?
  • You can start with: Excuse me? It opens at what time?

Example: A: The museum is three blocks away. B: Sorry, it's how many blocks away?

reading.title: A weekend in San Mateo
reading.intro: Read the San Mateo tourist guide and answer the questions.
paragraphs: San Mateo is a small city with a lot to see. It is easy to get around because the center is small, and you can walk everywhere. There is a big market, a museum, an old church and a lovely park. There are also many cafés, and some of them have free Wi-Fi.

Here is a short walking tour. The tour begins at the Central Plaza. Walk north on Hidalgo Street for two blocks. The museum is on the corner of Hidalgo and Juárez, across from the bank. It is closed on Mondays. Then turn right on Juárez Street and go straight ahead for three blocks. The market is on the left, next to a big bakery. It is great for shopping: you can buy shoes, bags and jewelry.

After the market, continue east on Juárez Street. At the end of the street, you can see the park. There is a small lake in the park, and there are some boats. Is there a place to eat near the lake? Yes, there is one. It's behind the lake, between a deli and a drugstore. Finally, walk back to the plaza on Morelos Street. If you need help, don't be shy. People in San Mateo are friendly, and they love to give directions. Can you find your way?
